department: Department of Agricultural Science and Engineering

deadline.value: International applicants abroad have an April 1 Fall priority deadline (June 1 for international applicants in the U.S.; July 1 general Fall priority); the program page notes doctoral deadlines are typically earlier than master's programs and should be confirmed with the Graduate School.
deadline.quote: Priority application deadlines for international applicants: | Fall Semester April 1 June 1

also.quote: Application deadlines for doctoral programs are typically earlier than master’s programs.

gre_general.value: Minimum GRE score of 290 required (Verbal + Quantitative, or Verbal, Quantitative & Subject).
gre_general.quote: Minimum GRE score of 290 (Verbal + Quantitative, or Verbal, Quantitative & Subject).

gre_subject.value: ETS offers GRE Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology (none in environmental or agricultural sciences).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: A faculty advisor aligned with the student's chosen concentration must be identified prior to admission and must accept the student.
supervisor.quote: A faculty advisor must be identified prior to admission, and the advisor must accept the student.

funding.value: Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA) support at the Ph.D. level is standard for 36 months; Graduate School and Title III assistantships provide monthly stipends ($3,000/month under Title III) and tuition coverage/in-state tuition.
funding.quote: Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA) at the Ph.D. level is standard for 36 months.

also.quote: Appointments provide a monthly stipend and most include tuition and fees.
$3,000 monthly stipend for doctoral students | In-state tuition while under contract

entry_route.value: Requires both a four-year bachelor's degree and a thesis-based M.S. degree (minimum 3.0 M.S. GPA) in an agricultural, food, biological, environmental, or related science.
entry_route.quote: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year degree-granting college or university AND a thesis-based M.S. degree with a major in an agricultural, food, biological, environmental, or related science.

notes: Ph.D. in Food, Agricultural and Environmental Sciences (48 credits post-M.S.) offers three concentrations: Natural Resources (environmental sciences, ecology, soils, forestry, geospatial analysis, climate), Plant Science, and Food and Animal Sciences.
name: Food, Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Ph.D.
